dedupe_keys.name: cartagena spain optimal routes for selective plastic waste collection with net2plan gis

description: This case study plans optimal routes for collecting plastic waste from selective collection bins in Cartagena, Spain. The authors, researchers at the Universidad Politécnica de Cartagena, developed a path planning algorithm that minimises environmental impact (carbon dioxide emissions and noise) and socio-economic cost (number of trucks and fuel use), and ran it in Net2Plan, an open-source network planning tool usually used for communication networks, extended with the Net2Plan-GIS library that imports the city layout and smart bin positions from geographic information system databases; the work is published as an open-access journal article, with the algorithm, tool and extension released as open source in a public repository. Coverage is one city. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the case covers plastic collection only, and the benefit depends on bin fill data and the chosen weights. The study showed that the platform computes optimal collection routes for the city and can feed urban mobility plans, and that it can be extended to other smart city routing problems. Simulation uses: a reusable open workflow for waste collection routing from GIS data. Related records: Net2Plan (platform-net2plan) is the planning tool used.
